# PokePay Deposit Complete Guide: How to Fund Your Crypto Virtual Card? Which Coins & Networks Are Supported? Top-Up Fees, Time & Common Issues Explained (Full PokePay Card Lineup & Latest Fee Comparison Inside)

So you typed "PokePay deposit" into the search bar. Chances are, you're sitting in one of three camps right now. Maybe you just registered an account and you're staring at the deposit screen wondering which network to pick. Maybe you sent USDT half an hour ago and the balance hasn't moved, and you're quietly panicking. Or maybe you're weighing up whether PokePay is even worth opening before you commit a single dollar of crypto to it.

All three are fair. The deposit step is where most new PokePay users hit their first friction — not because the platform is broken, but because the documentation is scattered, the fee details are buried in third-party reviews, and the difference between picking TRC20 versus ERC20 can mean the difference between a 30-cent top-up and a 12-dollar one.

This guide walks through the deposit process end to end, then layers in the card lineup and fee structure so you can decide whether PokePay earns a spot in your crypto-spending toolkit. No hype, no fluff — just the details you actually need before you tap "Confirm".

## What Is PokePay, In One Paragraph

PokePay is a Hong Kong-issued Visa prepaid card platform built for people who hold crypto and want to spend it without manually converting to fiat first. You top up with USDT, USDC, BTC, or ETH; the platform handles the crypto-to-fiat conversion on the backend; you swipe a virtual or physical Visa card at any of 130 million+ merchants worldwide. The company holds licenses in Hong Kong (MSO), Canada (FINTRAC MSB), and Poland (VASP), which puts it a notch above the no-license virtual card shops that pop up and disappear every few months. The product lineup splits into personal cards (virtual and physical) and business solutions (BaaS, VA accounts, OTC). For most readers searching "PokePay deposit", the personal virtual card is the entry point — so that's where we'll spend most of our time.

## PokePay Deposit: The Core Mechanics

### Supported Deposit Coins

PokePay accepts four cryptocurrencies for top-up:

- **USDT** (Tether) — the workhorse, lowest friction, most users go this route
- **USDC** — second most popular, similar UX to USDT
- **BTC** (Bitcoin) — supported but slower and more expensive due to network fees
- **ETH** (Ethereum) — supported but also gas-heavy

The card itself settles in HKD by default (the issuing bank is Hong Kong-based), with USD and EUR also supported. So when you deposit USDT, the platform converts it to your card's base currency before it lands as spendable balance. You don't see the conversion happen — it's automatic — but it's worth knowing the conversion spread exists.

### Supported Networks (Pick Wisely)

This is the part that catches people out. PokePay's app gives you a deposit address per coin, but the network you use to send matters more than the coin itself.

The practical advice from experienced users: **prefer TRC20 (TRON) or Avalanche C-Chain for USDT**. TRC20 transfers typically cost a fraction of a dollar in gas; C-Chain is similarly cheap. ERC20 (Ethereum mainnet) can run you $5–$15 per transfer just in network fees — and that's before any platform-side charge.

> **Note on network transparency:** PokePay does not publish a clear list of which chains are supported for top-up on its public-facing pages. Multiple users have reported top-up issues when sending via an unsupported network. Before transferring any meaningful amount, confirm the supported network with in-app prompts or support. Sending on the wrong network can mean lost funds.

### Deposit Time

PokePay's official line on settlement time is that deposits typically arrive within roughly 15 minutes. If more than 30 minutes pass without the balance updating, the platform recommends contacting customer support through the in-app chat.

In practice, TRC20 USDT deposits tend to land faster — usually under 5 minutes once the blockchain confirms. ETH and BTC deposits take longer because the underlying networks themselves are slower. Plan around 15–30 minutes as a realistic window, and don't panic if it takes a bit longer during network congestion.

## Step-by-Step: How to Deposit Into PokePay

If you're starting from zero, here's the full flow from registration to funded card.

1. **Register an account** through the [👉 PokePay invitation page](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) — using an invitation link during signup unlocks a discount coupon (currently around $12.8 off) that drops the virtual card activation fee from $20 to about $7.20.
2. **Complete minimal KYC** — typically a selfie plus basic identity info. Level 1 KYC is enough to unlock the virtual card; the physical card requires Level 2 KYC (ID document + face verification).
3. **Open the deposit page** inside the PokePay app — tap the "Import" / "Deposit" button on the home screen.
4. **Pick your coin and copy the deposit address** — the app shows you a unique per-coin address. Double-check the first and last 6 characters before sending.
5. **Send from your exchange (OKX, Binance, etc.)** — withdraw USDT (or whichever coin) to the copied address, selecting the matching network. Mismatched networks are the #1 cause of lost deposits.
6. **Wait for blockchain confirmation** — usually 15 minutes for USDT on TRC20. The balance updates automatically once the transaction confirms.
7. **Apply for your virtual card** — once the account is funded, tap "Card" → "Apply for card" → choose virtual (instant) or physical (ships in 10–30 business days from the Greater Bay Area).
8. **Activate and add to Apple Pay / Google Pay** — your CVV and card details appear in-app; you can bind to mobile wallets immediately and start spending.

For most users, the whole loop from sign-up to first successful payment takes under 30 minutes if everything goes smoothly.

## PokePay Deposit Fees: What You Actually Pay

Here's where the picture gets a bit murky, and honesty matters more than confidence. There are two layers of cost on every deposit, and sources disagree on one of them.

**Layer 1 — Blockchain network fee (gas):** This is paid to miners/validators, not to PokePay. It varies by network. TRC20: typically under $1. C-Chain: similar. ERC20: $5–$15 depending on Ethereum congestion. BTC and ETH mainnet transfers: comparable. This fee is unavoidable on any crypto platform.

**Layer 2 — Platform top-up fee:** Here's the conflict. The most detailed third-party review (ucardcrypto's 2026 evaluation) lists a **1% recharge fee** on all crypto top-ups. Another detailed third-party fee breakdown claims **PokePay charges no platform fee on deposits — gas only**. The official PokePay FAQ and product pages do not state a specific deposit fee percentage publicly.

How to handle this in practice:

- Treat **1% as the conservative assumption** when modelling your costs.
- Confirm the current rate inside the app's deposit screen before sending a meaningful amount, since promotional periods or account tiers may change the effective fee.
- Either way, gas-only or 1%-plus-gas, the deposit cost on TRC20 is still low single-digit dollars for a typical $100–$500 top-up.

The reason this matters is that the deposit fee stacks with the spending fee. The realistic per-transaction cost on PokePay once you've topped up and made a purchase is somewhere around **2% combined** (1% spend fee + 1% FX fee on non-HKD transactions), plus whatever you paid on the deposit side. For subscriptions and occasional online shopping, that's tolerable. For daily high-volume spending, it adds up.

## The Full PokePay Card Lineup: What You Can Actually Get

PokePay runs multiple card segments (BINs) — some Visa, some Mastercard, with different fee profiles. The table below consolidates what's known from the platform and detailed third-party breakdowns. Prices marked "with invitation" reflect the discount unlocked by registering through the [👉 PokePay invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) before applying for a card.

| Card Segment | Network | Activation Fee | Monthly Fee | Annual Fee | Transaction Fee | FX Fee | Cross-Border Fee | Min Top-Up | Get This Card |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PokeCard (new Visa, 2024) | Visa | $20 standard / ~$7.2 with invitation | $0 | $0 | 1% | 1% | 0% | ~$30 | [ Apply via invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |
| 559666 segment | Mastercard | $20 | $0 | $0 | 1% | 0% | 0.5% | ~$20 | [ Apply via invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |
| 404038 segment | Visa | $20 | $0 | $0 | 1% | 0% | 1% | ~$20 | [ Apply via invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |
| 556150 segment (budget) | Mastercard | $5 | $1/month | $0 | 1% | 0% | 0.5% | ~$10 | [ Apply via invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |
| 441112 segment (budget) | Visa | $5 | $1/month | $0 | 1% | 0% | 1% | ~$10 | [ Apply via invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |
| Physical Card | Visa | $88 standard / ~$70 with invitation | $0 | $0 | 1% | 1% | 0% | ~$30 | [ Apply for physical card](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) |

A few things worth calling out about this table:

- **The "as low as $5" headline on PokePay's homepage refers to the budget segments** (556150 Mastercard and 441112 Visa). Those carry a $1/month fee instead of zero. The flagship PokeCard (the 2024-launched Visa) is the one with $0 monthly fees but a $20 activation fee, which drops to ~$7.2 with the invitation discount.
- **Cross-border fee differences are real and worth picking based on your use case.** If you spend mostly in HKD or with Hong Kong merchants, the 0% cross-border PokeCard is the cheapest. If you spend internationally in USD/EUR, the 559666 Mastercard with 0.5% cross-border and 0% FX may actually beat the headline PokeCard on net cost.
- **The physical card is the same card segment as the flagship virtual Visa, just in plastic form.** Same fee structure, plus ATM withdrawal support (typically 2% per withdrawal, with a HKD 5,000 daily ATM cap and a max of 5 ATM withdrawals per day). The full daily spending limit across all cards is HKD 100,000 (around $12,500 USD) per day.

PokePay's official positioning on the homepage pushes "0% cross-border transaction fees, 0 monthly fees, 0 annual fees, no micro-transaction fees" — those claims apply specifically to the flagship PokeCard Visa segment, not to every segment in the table above. Read the segment details before assuming the marketing line applies to whichever card you end up with.

## Common PokePay Deposit Problems & How to Fix Them

Let's run through the issues that show up most often in user reports and community threads.

### "I deposited but my balance hasn't updated"

Wait at least 30 minutes. TRC20 USDT usually confirms within 5–10 minutes, but during network congestion or platform-side batching, it can stretch. If 30 minutes have passed and the blockchain explorer shows your transaction as confirmed, open a support ticket through in-app chat. Don't send a second deposit hoping the first one will catch up — that just creates two pending transfers to track.

### "I picked the wrong network"

This is the worst-case scenario. If you sent USDT on ERC20 to a TRC20 deposit address (or vice versa), the funds may be irrecoverable. PokePay's support can sometimes recover cross-network sends if the platform technically supports both networks for that coin, but it is not guaranteed and can take weeks. Always double-check the network selector on your exchange before confirming the withdrawal.

### "My deposit triggered an account review"

Some users report that their account gets flagged for compliance review after a deposit, especially larger ones. This is standard KYC/AML procedure on smaller fintech platforms, not a fee issue. The fix is to complete identity verification thoroughly ahead of time — upload a clear ID, take a clean selfie, fill in your name exactly as it appears on your ID. Passport-registered users should use the English name as printed on the passport.

### "The deposit fee was higher than I expected"

This is almost always gas, not PokePay. Check the network you used. If you sent on ERC20, that's your problem — switch to TRC20 for future deposits. If you sent on TRC20 and the deduction was still notable, it may include a 1% platform fee (see the fee section above for the uncertainty there). Confirm the current fee inside the app's deposit screen.

### "My card got declined after I deposited"

Usually a 3DS or merchant-side issue, not a deposit issue. Make sure 3D Secure is toggled on in the PokePay app (it's required by many international merchants), make sure your card is unlocked (PokePay has a one-click lock/unlock toggle), and confirm the merchant isn't on the unsupported list — Steam, OpenAI/ChatGPT, and a handful of others have historically had issues with the Hong Kong-issued PokePay BIN. Apple Store, Google Play, PayPal, Netflix, Spotify, Alipay HK, and Wise generally work fine.

## PokePay Deposit: Realistic Cost Walkthrough

To make this concrete, here's what a typical small user's first month might look like.

Say you top up **$100 USDT on TRC20**, with an assumed 1% platform fee plus ~$0.30 in gas. You're out $1.30 before you've spent anything. Your card balance lands at roughly $98.70.

You subscribe to ChatGPT Plus at $20/month — wait, scratch that, PokePay's HK-issued card has been blocked by OpenAI. Let's pick something that works. You subscribe to Netflix Premium at $22.99, buy a $30 item on eBay, and load $20 into your PayPal wallet. Total spend: $72.99. Transaction fees at 1%: $0.73. FX fee at 1% (assuming all non-HKD): another $0.73. So you've spent $72.99 and paid $1.46 in fees on top of the $1.30 from deposit — total cost of using the card this month: $2.76 on $73 of spending, roughly 3.8%.

That's the honest math. Not bad for occasional use, not great if you're running $2,000 a month through it. The card sits dormant without monthly fees during months you don't use it, which is the real upside for low-frequency users.

## Where PokePay Deposit & Cards Fit vs Alternatives

If you're shopping around, it's worth knowing where PokePay sits in the broader crypto card landscape.

- **Lower fees on spending:** Tevau charges 1% on top-ups but 0% on spending transactions, and supports daily limits up to $3,000,000 versus PokePay's ~$12,500. Better fit for high-volume users.
- **Higher limits:** RedotPay supports up to $1,000,000 per day with full KYC. Better fit for freelancers and remote workers moving meaningful volume.
- **Cashback:** Ether.fi Cash offers 3% cashback in wETH; Bybit offers up to 10% for eligible users. PokePay has no dedicated cashback programme — only a referral/node program that pays up to 50% commission on referred users' fees.
- **Cheaper physical card:** Bybit's physical card costs $5; SafePal's is free. PokePay's physical card at $88 (or $70 with invitation) is among the more expensive in the category.

PokePay's genuine advantages are **fast onboarding (virtual card in under 10 minutes)**, **zero monthly fees**, **Apple Pay and Google Pay support from day one**, and **integration with Alipay HK, WeChat Pay, PayPal, Wise, and major subscription platforms**. For an entry-level crypto card user who wants something that just works for online shopping and subscriptions, the deposit friction is minimal and the card activation cost is genuinely low with the invitation discount.

## Restricted Regions — Check Before You Deposit

PokePay does not operate globally. The restricted jurisdictions list includes (among others): **United States, Russia, mainland China, Iraq, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Sudan, Syria, Afghanistan, Belarus, Myanmar, Pakistan, Lebanon, Yemen, Somalia, Ethiopia, Libya, Venezuela, Zimbabwe**, and parts of the Balkans.

If you're in any of those regions, depositing crypto into PokePay is a waste — you'll be blocked from using the card. Hong Kong, most of Southeast Asia, Europe (outside restricted countries), Canada, and Latin America are generally fine. Confirm on the platform's restricted regions prompt at signup before committing funds.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How long does a PokePay deposit take?**
Officially around 15 minutes. In practice, TRC20 USDT deposits usually confirm in 5–10 minutes. If 30+ minutes pass with no update, contact support.

**What's the minimum deposit amount?**
The minimum top-up per transaction is 0.1 HKD (~$0.013 USD). Practical minimums are higher because gas fees on any network will eat a micro-deposit. Most users send at least $20–$30 to make the gas worthwhile.

**Is there a maximum deposit?**
PokePay advertises no upper cap on top-up amount. The daily *spending* limit is HKD 100,000 (~$12,500 USD) per day across all transactions.

**Does PokePay charge a deposit fee?**
Third-party reviews cite a 1% recharge fee. Other detailed breakdowns claim no platform fee, gas only. The official PokePay pages don't publicly specify a deposit fee percentage. Confirm inside the app before sending a large amount.

**Can I deposit fiat currency (USD/EUR bank transfer)?**
Personal users primarily deposit via crypto. Business users get access to VA (Virtual Account) services that support SWIFT, SEPA, ACH, and IBAN fiat rails. For personal card top-up, crypto is the standard route.

**What happens if I send crypto to the wrong address?**
Funds sent to a wrong address are almost certainly unrecoverable. Always verify the first and last 6 characters of the deposit address before confirming the withdrawal on your exchange.

**Can I withdraw my balance back to crypto?**
Yes. Withdrawals go back to your own crypto wallet and incur only network gas fees (per the most detailed third-party breakdowns). No platform-side withdrawal percentage fee is documented, though you should confirm current terms in-app.

## Final Take

PokePay earns its place as a starter crypto card for users who want fast onboarding, zero monthly fees, and a working Apple Pay / Google Pay / PayPal / Alipay experience without much fuss. The deposit process itself is straightforward once you pick the right network — TRC20 USDT, ~15 minutes, modest gas. The fees on the spend side (~2% combined for international users) are the real cost to weigh, and they make PokePay better suited to occasional subscriptions and online shopping than to daily high-volume spending.

If you're going to give it a shot, register through the [👉 PokePay invitation link](https://bit.ly/PoKePay) to unlock the activation discount, complete KYC level 1 before you deposit anything, send your first top-up on TRC20 with a small test amount (say $20–$30) to confirm the flow works end-to-end, and only then move larger balances. That's the boring, unglamorous, genuinely useful advice — and it'll save you the kind of mistakes that turn "PokePay deposit" from a quick search into a multi-day support ticket.
